text:
GENERATE BURST KP-B1c — THE ESTABLISHING IMAGE: the whole Crucible arena — the crusader cathedral's nave, sacked this week — and the world around it, BARE (Run KC2-PLAY; conductor gandalf; Matt: "we made them open scenes to start off with (no trees, rocks, etc) and added them later as we went — this helped to plan the space"). task_id "KP-B1c".

WHAT THIS IS. One 1536x1024 painted overview of the ENTIRE playable arena and its surroundings, composed as our fixed game camera would see it if it could pull back: elevated three-quarter view, 52.95 degrees down, north is screen-up, no perspective vanishing point (parallel projection). IMAGE 1 is the geometry guide of the whole floor plate at this overview scale: the measured arena outline (a tall ring, gate gap at the top = north), four interior islands (fallen pillar bases), six pool hazards (hatched discs). THE OUTLINE IS A SUGGESTION: the art decides where the walls and structures go; keep the overall footprint, the north gate, the islands and the pools roughly where the guide puts them.

BARE SCENE RULE (this is the point of this image): paint ONLY the architecture and the ground — the nave floor, the walls and their faces, the dais and altar steps, the piers and arcades, the breaches, the crypt openings, the collapsed vault sections, the transepts and side chapels, the ruined facade at the south end — and the world beyond the walls. NO dressing: no furniture, no pews, no statues, no candles, no bodies, no bone piles, no banners, no gates or iron fences, no scattered rubble props. Those are added later as separate objects so the space can be planned first. Floor damage IS allowed and follows the crack law: one blast crater with radial cracks at the north gate, a few impact fractures where the vault fell, scorch where fire burned, and every other flagstone smooth and whole — no spiderweb cracks anywhere.

THE BUILDING (identity by qualities, never names): a fortress-cathedral of a crusading order that held a border against hell and lost it: mass before grace — enormous piers, Romanesque weight with gothic verticals, cold GREY-WHITE and BLACK dressed stone, IRON only where it is structural (bound doors, chains from the vault). A faith of the SUN and the CHAIN: a gold sun-disc's empty mount in the apse; sun sigils inlaid in the polished floor. This building was WHOLE a week ago: its floor is smooth and beautiful; the violence is local and legible. IMAGE 4 is a painted chunk of this same interior at full scale (its register, stone and light are right; ignore its furniture, gates, banners and piles — those were mistakes for this stage).

THE LAYOUT (north = up): the CHANCEL at the north end — a raised dais, the apse wall broken open at the top so the world shows through it; the long NAVE down the middle with arcades of piers left and right; TRANSEPTS east and west partway down; side CHAPELS behind the arcades; the collapsed SOUTH facade at the bottom, opening onto a forecourt. The WEST wall (screen left) is BREACHED from outside — the sunset floods in through it. Three or four CRYPT BREACHES in the floor (dark openings with cold blue-white light from below, stairs descending); two of them near where monsters would enter. The four islands are the bases of fallen piers. The six pool hazards are burning pitch seeping through broken flagstones.

BEYOND THE WALLS (this is the cliffside's world, seen from inside the building the player walked toward): through the broken apse to the NORTH — the open valley in violet mist at sunset, a river, and far off the cliff with a bridge, its west faces lit gold; through the WEST breach — the sun on the ridge, the crag's slope falling away; to the EAST — the transept's outer wall gone and burning outbuildings on the hillside; to the SOUTH — the forecourt, the road that climbs the crag, and the hillside. Above: broken vault ribs at the top edge.

LIGHT: sun setting in the WEST (screen left); GOLD light floods through the west breach and rakes EAST across the polished floor between the piers in long shafts; piers throw long violet-blue shadows; fire (crater, pools, behind the apse) is the ONLY saturated warm; the sunset is gold-amber and diffuse; ambient deep cool violet-blue; shadows readable, never pure black.

REGISTER (frozen): HAND-DRAWN painted 2D exactly as IMAGE 3 (our cliffside level): confident dark contour with visible taper and varying weight, painted fills in clean planes, restrained texture, readable silhouettes, no conspicuous brush or pixel grain; not pixel art, not cel-shaded, not a 3D render, not photoreal. IMAGE 2 is the same cathedral seen from outside, burning: match its stone and fire. No text, no UI, no figures, no grid.

DELIVER exactly ONE 1536x1024 image_gen result in EDIT mode over IMAGE 1. ONE retry only if: dressing objects appear (furniture, bodies, gates, statues), the floor carries spiderweb cracks, the world beyond the walls is missing, the register drifts from IMAGE 3, or the layout does not read (chancel north, nave, transepts, south facade) — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/b1c_establishing_01.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "KP-B1c"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED; concerns listed honestly. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — geometry guide of the WHOLE floor plate at overview scale (outline = suggestion; gate north; four islands; six pool discs) — EDIT target
IMAGE 2 — the same cathedral from outside, burning (identity, stone, fire)
IMAGE 3 — register exemplar: our painted cliffside level (match the hand exactly)
IMAGE 4 — a full-scale painted chunk of this interior (register/stone/light right; ignore its furniture, gates, banners, piles)
